name: Oxabolone

card.summary: An obscure nandrolone-family anabolic steroid that was never marketed itself and is banned in sport, with almost no published research.
card.note: Prohibited by WADA; one case report links it to mucosal hyperpigmentation.

quick.overview:
Oxabolone is an anabolic steroid related to nandrolone. The parent compound was never sold as a drug, though an injectable ester called oxabolone cipionate has been used medically.

Very little has been published about it. No trials of its effects on muscle or appearance were found.
quick.mechanism: As an anabolic-androgenic steroid it is classed as an androgen receptor agonist, but encyclopedic sources give no details of its potency or metabolism.
quick.risks: It is on the WADA prohibited list. A 1995 case report described mucosal hyperpigmentation associated with it; no broader safety data were found.

lead: Oxabolone (4-hydroxy-19-nortestosterone) is a synthetic anabolic-androgenic steroid in the nandrolone (19-nortestosterone) group.[1] Compounds in this class are used by some bodybuilders for the muscle size and leaner physique they associate with anabolic steroids, and oxabolone is discussed in that context, mostly as a rare or hard-to-find member of the family.[3][4]

The parent compound was never marketed itself; its cipionate ester, oxabolone cipionate, has been marketed for medical use as an intramuscular injection.[1] T Nation forum posts describe it under the older brand name Steranabol and list oxabolone cipionate in brand tables of injectable steroids.[2][6]

Oxabolone is on the World Anti-Doping Agency's list of prohibited substances and is banned in most major sports; anti-doping and workplace urine-screening panels reproduced in forum threads list it and its metabolite.[1][5][7] Published literature is sparse. No clinical trials of its muscle or appearance effects were located; the only indexed human report concerns a skin and mucosal side effect.[8]

chain: Anabolic androgen-receptor signalling, as with related steroids
Claimed: greater muscle mass and a leaner look
angle.text: Users of nandrolone-type steroids seek increased muscle size and a harder physique, and oxabolone is discussed as one more compound of that type. No trial has measured these effects for oxabolone specifically.[3][4]

paras: Oxabolone is a 19-nortestosterone derivative carrying a hydroxyl group at the 4-position.[1] Related compounds include its 17-alpha-methylated analogue methylhydroxynandrolone and a further methylated derivative, oxymesterone.[1]

Oxabolone is listed among substances prohibited in sport by the World Anti-Doping Agency, and encyclopedic sources describe no mainstream therapeutic use of the parent compound.[1] Forum threads show it on lists of banned or screened steroids, including a thread on natural bodybuilding contest rules and one on an overseas job urine test.[5][7]

In T Nation threads, users have described oxabolone as a compound they would like to see available: a 2006 poster wished someone would make oxabolone cypionate, and a 2020 poster hoped for oxabolone and stenbolone to become available, saying they had read an account of oxabolone from the 1980s.[3][4] A 2002 poster said a supplement called Testobol had the same chemical structure as oxabolone, which they said had been manufactured as Steranabol, and suggested the product might be breaking rules.[6] These are user statements and were not verified.
A 1995 case report in Acta Dermato-Venereologica described mucosal hyperpigmentation attributed to oxabolone.[8] Beyond this report, no systematic safety data were located.
No studies found. The only human literature identified is the single case report of mucosal hyperpigmentation.[8]

timeline.event: Case report of mucosal hyperpigmentation attributed to oxabolone is published.[8]

lore.intro: On T Nation, oxabolone appears mainly as a rarely available nandrolone-class steroid that members mention wishing to see, and in lists of banned substances.[3][4][5]

claims.claim: Oxabolone is a desirable, hard-to-find nandrolone-type steroid.
claims.believers: Posters in 2006 and 2020 expressed a wish for oxabolone cypionate or oxabolone to become available, one citing an account from the 1980s.[3][4]
claims.experts: Encyclopedic sources report oxabolone cipionate was marketed for medical use and that the compound is prohibited in sport; no trials of its muscle effects were located.[1]

claims.claim: A supplement product matched oxabolone's chemical structure.
claims.believers: A 2002 poster said the product Testobol had the same structure as oxabolone, formerly sold as Steranabol.[6]
claims.experts: No regulatory or published analysis of that product was located.
